intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries such as Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor near Guia, sampling regional varieties including Negra Mole and Arinto. Guided tours include vineyard walks, cellar visits, and curated tastings of 5–7 wines paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil into the famous Algar de Benagil sea cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves with a natural skylight dome. A guided 2-hour kayak experience lets you explore hidden grottos and sea arches along the dramatic coastline.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Barrier Island Tour
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, stopping at pristine barrier island beaches like Ilha Deserta and Ilha do Farol. Enjoy untouched white-sand beaches, spot flamingos and migratory birds, and sample fresh local oysters harvested directly from the lagoon.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour through the charming historic town of Tavira, sampling local Algarve wines from small producers alongside traditional petiscos (Portuguese tapas) such as cataplana de marisco, carob liqueur, and almond sweets at curated local taverns and wine bars.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly bus (Eva/Rede Expressos) or shared shuttle to Lagoa/Carvoeiro area (~€10-15). Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay at Praia da Marinha. Take a gentle orientation walk along the clifftop paths above Praia da Marinha to get your bearings and enjoy the stunning golden limestone rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll down to Praia da Marinha beach for a sunset view over the iconic sea stacks and grottos. Relax and decompress from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during travel — grab a pastel de nata and coffee at a café kiosk (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Pick up groceries or a sandwich from a local mini-mercado near the accommodation (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: O Pescador restaurant in Carvoeiro village (~3km away) — try grilled sardines or catch of the day, budget meal ~€10-14 per person

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm (24-27°C) with less crowds than peak summer. Buy a reusable water bottle to save money. Get a local SIM or check roaming options for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim and exploration of Praia da Marinha — one of Portugal's most beautiful beaches. Walk the coastal boardwalk trail eastward toward Praia do Carvalho. The sea caves and arches are spectacular at low tide. Bring snorkeling gear if possible (rentable locally for ~€5-8).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a local bus to nearby Benagil Beach (~4km). Join a budget kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour to enter the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) — book in advance, costs ~€15-20 per person. This is one of the Algarve's most iconic sights.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for the evening. Browse the whitewashed streets, visit the small chapel overlook, and watch the sunset from Carvoeiro's main beach cliff.

meals.breakfast: Café Paraíso or any local pastelaria in Lagoa — coffee, toast, and pastel de nata (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl in Lagoa) — bread, cheese, local ham, fruit (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Zé in Carvoeiro or similar local tasca — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and house wine (~€12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Benagil kayak tours the evening before as they sell out quickly even in September. Wear reef shoes for rocky beach entries.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Portimão (~15km, ~€2.50). Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão) — housed in a former sardine canning factory, entry is free or very low cost (~€3). Fascinating history of the Algarve fishing industry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge or take a short ferry (~€1) to Ferragudo village — a charming, less touristy fishing village with a castle (Castelo de São João do Arade), narrow cobblestone streets, and beautiful views over the Arade River estuary. Explore on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the sunset from Ferragudo's small beach (Praia Grande de Ferragudo). Return to Portimão by ferry and bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation or local café in Lagoa (~€3-5)
meals.lunch: A Taberna da Maré in Ferragudo — riverside casual dining, grilled fish of the day (~€10-13 per person)
meals.dinner: Cook at accommodation using fresh ingredients from Portimão's daily market (Mercado Municipal) — fresh fish, vegetables, local bread (~€8-10 for two)

day_by_day.notes: Portimão market is open mornings only — buy fresh fish and produce before heading to Ferragudo. Ferragudo is one of the Algarve's hidden gems and very photogenic.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a bus or taxi (~€10 one way) to Lagoa town center, which is the heart of Algarve wine production. Visit Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) or Quinta dos Vales — many offer free or low-cost tastings (~€5-10) of local Algarve wines including the regional DOC Lagoa wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine trail — visit Adega Cooperativa do Algarve in Lagoa, one of the oldest cooperatives in the region. Taste local white, red, and the famous medronho (arbutus berry brandy). Purchase a bottle of local wine for ~€5-8 to enjoy at the accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha area. Enjoy a leisurely evening with your purchased wine watching the sunset from the clifftops.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Lagoa town — galão (milky coffee) and croissant (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Mirante in Lagoa — daily lunch special (prato do dia) including soup, main, and drink (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Light dinner at accommodation — local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), olives, bread, and your winery purchase (~€6-8)

day_by_day.notes: Call wineries ahead to confirm tasting availability and hours. September is harvest season — you may catch grape harvesting activities, which is a special experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus to Lagos (~25km, ~€3.50). Explore the historic old town: walk the ancient city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António (free or ~€2), and the Mercado de Lagos for local produce and crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — the most dramatic coastal rock formation in the Algarve. Hike the clifftop trail and take the steps down to the water level grottos. Optionally rent a kayak from the beach below (~€15/hour) to explore sea caves independently.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lagos waterfront promenade (Avenida dos Descobrimentos). Browse the lively Saturday evening atmosphere and enjoy the town's vibrant energy.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation before departing
meals.lunch: : Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — affordable Portuguese cuisine near the marina, prato do dia ~€9-12
meals.dinner: A Forja restaurant in Lagos old town — known for generous portions of traditional Algarvian food (~€12-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos has excellent nightlife if you want to enjoy a Saturday evening out. The bus back to Lagoa runs until late evening. Ponta da Piedade is best in afternoon light for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. Early swim before crowds arrive. Explore the rock pools and hidden coves accessible by scrambling along the cliffs at low tide (check tide tables). Practice snorkeling in the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia de Albandeira (~2km east) — a quieter, smaller cove beach with a natural arch. Walk the Via Algarviana coastal trail segment between the two beaches for stunning views. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Sunday evening is quiet — enjoy a slow evening in Carvoeiro. Visit the Galeria Bar on the cliffs for a sunset drink (one drink budget ~€4-6).

meals.breakfast: Cook at accommodation — eggs, toast, local jam, coffee (~€3-4 in groceries)
meals.lunch: Beach picnic — visit the local mini-mercado for fresh bread, tuna, olives, and local snacks (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — Sunday roast-style Portuguese meal, generous portions (~€11-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is a good rest day. Many shops close early. Tide tables are available free online — low tide opens up spectacular rock pools and cave access at Marinha.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (~20km north). Take the train from Tunes or bus from Lagoa (~€3-5 return). Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves, ~€3 entry) and the Gothic Cathedral (Sé de Silves, free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town on foot — browse the Tuesday market area (may have stalls), visit the Museu Arqueológico de Silves (~€2). Walk along the Arade River banks and enjoy the quiet, authentic Portuguese town atmosphere far from the beach crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa/Marinha area by bus or train. Cook dinner at accommodation with produce bought at Silves.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at accommodation before early departure
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves (inside castle gardens) — affordable local food with a view (~€9-12), or Restaurante Marisqueira Rui — known for grilled chicken and local dishes (~€10-13)
meals.dinner: Home cooked meal using Silves market produce — traditional caldo verde soup and local sausage (~€5-7 in ingredients)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a fantastic contrast to the coastal scene — authentic, historical, and very affordable. The castle views over the orange groves and Arade River valley are beautiful. September orange harvest is beginning.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia do Carvalho — a hidden gem beach accessible only through a tunnel carved into the cliff (~2km walk from Marinha). Arrive early for the best experience. Bring snorkeling gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the full Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a stunning 11km coastal clifftop walk from Praia do Vale de Centeanes to Praia da Marinha. This is one of Portugal's most beautiful coastal hikes. Completely free and breathtaking.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recovery after the hike. Light evening walk in Carvoeiro. Visit a local pharmacy if needed for any sunburn or muscle aches.

meals.breakfast: Energy-rich breakfast at accommodation — porridge, fruit, yogurt (~€3-4 in groceries)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch for the trail — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, energy bars (~€5-7 prepared the night before)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nortada in Carvoeiro — grilled fish and salad, simple and fresh (~€11-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike early morning (before 9am) to avoid heat and crowds. Wear proper walking shoes, bring 2L water minimum, sunscreen, and a hat. The trail is well-marked with yellow arrows.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting excursion — take a bus or taxi to Quinta de Penina or Quinta do Morgado da Torre near Portimão. These estates offer estate tours and tastings focusing on Algarve red wines and rosés (~€8-15 for a tasting flight). Book ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mexilhoeira Grande village near Portimão — a quiet authentic Algarvian village. Stop at local olive oil producers and taste locally pressed olive oil (often free samples). Browse the village and enjoy the rural Algarve atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão for the evening. Walk along the Portimão riverfront promenade and enjoy the fishing harbor atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — toasted muffin, cheese, ham, coffee (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: At the winery if they offer a food pairing option, or packed lunch (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Portimão — famous for affordable petiscos and local wine, very popular with locals (~€10-13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Algarve wines are underrated and very affordable to buy directly from the producer. September is harvest season so wineries are particularly active and welcoming. Buy a few bottles to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Armação de Pêra and Praia Grande (~15km, bus ~€2.50). Armação de Pêra has one of the longest beaches in the Algarve. Walk the full beach length and explore the small old fishing quarter with its 17th-century chapel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east by bus to Albufeira (~25km total from Lagoa, ~€4). Visit the old town (Albufeira Velha) — the historic fishing village core is charming despite the touristy surroundings. Walk down to Praia dos Pescadores (Fisherman's Beach) in the old town cove.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira old town's evening atmosphere. The Rua Cândido dos Reis pedestrian strip has many affordable restaurants. Return to Lagoa by bus (~€3).

meals.breakfast: At accommodation
meals.lunch: A Ruína restaurant in Albufeira old town — iconic cliffside location, fresh fish at moderate prices (~€12-15 per person, splurge slightly)
meals.dinner: Pick up takeaway piri piri chicken from a local churrascaria in Albufeira for the bus ride (~€7-9)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is more touristy but the old town is genuinely historic and worth seeing. Avoid the Strip area (Avenida Sa Carneiro) which is very commercialized. Focus on the old town and beach.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning at Praia da Marinha. Final dedicated beach morning — swim, sunbathe, snorkel, and enjoy this world-class beach. Explore any remaining rock formations and sea arches you haven't visited.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lagoa town's weekly market (check local schedule) for fresh produce, local honey, figs, almonds, and Algarvian sweets (Dom Rodrigos, Morgados). Stock up on affordable local food souvenirs. Visit the Adega Cooperativa one more time to purchase wine to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at accommodation — fresh fruit, yogurt, local pastries (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Market snacks and fresh produce picnic at a shaded spot in Lagoa town square (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo (return visit) — one of the best fish restaurants in the area, order the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) to share (~€15-18 per person, special occasion)

day_by_day.notes: Buy vacuum-packed local products at the market — medronho, local wine, fig and almond sweets, and local olive oil make excellent affordable souvenirs within airline liquid rules.

day_by_day.morning: Final day trip — take a bus to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (~50km west, ~€7 one way). Cabo de São Vicente is the southwesternmost point of continental Europe — a dramatic, windswept headland with a lighthouse. Utterly spectacular and free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress, ~€3 entry) — the legendary base of Henry the Navigator and Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the dramatic cliffs and watch surfers at Praia do Tonel.
day_by_day.evening: Return by bus to Lagoa (~2 hours). Pack bags and prepare for departure. Final evening walk to Praia da Marinha cliffs for a last sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Restaurante Nortada in Sagres — fresh tuna steak (local specialty), very affordable (~€10-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Simple farewell meal at accommodation — use remaining groceries, toast with the last bottle of local wine

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is very windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The bus journey is long but scenic. Check return bus times carefully as evening services are limited. Book the morning bus early.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of accommodation. Take one last walk to Praia da Marinha for a farewell swim if time allows. Collect all luggage and arrange transfer to Faro Airport (bus via Portimão and Faro, ~€8-12, or shared shuttle ~€15-20). Allow 3+ hours for the journey and airport check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart from Faro Airport. Browse duty-free for any last-minute Portuguese wine, Compal juices, or pastéis de nata to enjoy on the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Flight home — carry memories of 13 incredible days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at a café near the accommodation — galão, pastel de nata, tosta mista (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring packed snacks from accommodation (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: On the flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): €400-550 per person, covering local transport (~€60), meals (~€200-250), activities and entrances (~€80-100), wine tastings (~€40-60), and miscellaneous (~€50). September offers ideal weather, lower prices than July-August, and thinner crowds — excellent choice of travel month.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, rent a car at Faro Airport (essential for Algarve exploration), and drive ~45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle first look at Praia da Marinha — one of Portugal's most iconic beaches, just steps from the hotel. Walk the clifftop trail for sweeping views of the golden limestone formations, sea arches, and turquoise coves. A short 15-minute walk down to the beach for a swim if energy allows.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearby village of Carvoeiro (~10 min drive) for a relaxed first evening. Explore the charming whitewashed village square and watch the sunset from the clifftop boardwalk.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at Faro Airport before departure.
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or a roadside café en route — try a Bifana (pork sandwich) or pastel de nata at a local padaria.
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant in Carvoeiro — mid-range seafood restaurant with terrace views. Try grilled sea bass (robalo) or the cataplana de marisco (seafood stew). Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Car rental is strongly recommended for the full 13 days. Book in advance for September. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. September in Algarve is warm (~26°C) with minimal crowds compared to August.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Praia da Marinha. Arrive early (~9:00) to claim a spot on this relatively small but stunning beach. Swim in the crystal-clear waters, explore the sea caves and rock formations by foot at low tide, and snorkel if you have gear (rentals available nearby).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 20 minutes west to Praia de Benagil. Take a kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour (book ahead) into the famous Benagil Sea Cave — one of the most photographed caves in the world. Tours typically last 1–2 hours and depart from Benagil beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lagoa area. Visit the town of Lagoa itself (~15 min drive) and explore the local wine cooperative — Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — one of the Algarve's most established wine producers. Evening wine tasting session (book ahead, ~€10–15 per person).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay or a local café — fresh fruit, toast with local honey, and galão (milky espresso).
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Benagil or a picnic — grab local cheeses, presunto (cured ham), and fresh bread from a Lagoa supermarket.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Pescador in Lagoa — beloved local spot for fresh grilled fish. Try the grilled dourada (gilt-head bream) with potatoes and salad. Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave boat tours sell out fast in September — book online at least 2–3 days ahead. Low tide is best for cave exploration. Bring reef shoes for rocky beach access at Marinha.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~30 minutes east to Silves, the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€3 entry) with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley. Visit the Gothic Cathedral of Silves next door.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves old town — browse the artisan shops, visit the Roman Bridge, and walk along the riverside. Drive 20 minutes south to Armação de Pêra beach for a relaxed afternoon swim on one of the Algarve's longest sandy beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro for the evening. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at one of the clifftop bars overlooking the beach, then dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Café Central in Silves town square — coffee and fresh pastries including the local Dom Rodrigos (almond and egg sweets).
meals.lunch: Café Ingles in Silves — charming mid-range restaurant in the castle gardens. Try the local orange and almond salad or a hearty açorda (bread soup).
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — cozy family-run restaurant with excellent grilled meats and fish. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a must-visit for history lovers. The castle is well-preserved and the views are spectacular. September is citrus harvest season — you may see orange and fig trees laden with fruit throughout the region.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~1 hour west to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Walk the dramatic clifftops (up to 75m high), visit the lighthouse, and feel the wild Atlantic winds. A deeply memorable, almost spiritual experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and the impressive Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry) — the fortress where Prince Henry the Navigator planned Portugal's Age of Discovery. Walk the clifftop perimeter and watch surfers tackle the powerful Atlantic waves at Praia do Tonel.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back east (~1.5 hrs) stopping for dinner in the charming town of Lagos — the gateway to the western Algarve. Explore Lagos old town with its Moorish walls and vibrant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the drive. Pack snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: A Sagres — simple seafood restaurant in Sagres village. Try the fresh tuna steak or grilled percebes (barnacles) — a local delicacy. Budget ~€15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: : Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — excellent traditional Portuguese cuisine in a rustic wine-cellar setting. Try the bacalhau à brás (shredded salt cod with eggs and potatoes). Budget ~€22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cabo de São Vicente is windy year-round — bring a light jacket even in September. The drive from Lagoa to Sagres is scenic along the EN125. Consider stopping at Praia de Salema or Praia do Burgau on the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos more thoroughly — visit the Ponta da Piedade, a stunning series of golden rock formations, grottos, and arches accessible by a clifftop walk (~2km) or by boat tour from Lagos marina. The boat tour (~€15–20) takes you through sea caves and arches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on one of Lagos's beautiful beaches — Meia Praia (long sandy beach north of the marina) or the more secluded Praia do Camilo (dramatic cove between cliffs). September crowds are manageable.
day_by_day.evening: Lagos has a vibrant Saturday evening scene. Walk the historic old town, visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), and enjoy the lively Rua 25 de Abril for bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Mó in Lagos — beloved local bakery for fresh pastries and coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach or a beachside café — grab local cheeses, olives, and fresh bread from the Saturday market in Lagos.
meals.dinner: No Pátio in Lagos — lovely courtyard restaurant with creative Portuguese-Mediterranean fusion. Try the tuna tataki or the Algarve-style clams (amêijoas à Bulhão Pato). Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Lagos has a lively Saturday market near the waterfront — great for local produce, honey, almonds, and handicrafts. Book Ponta da Piedade boat tours in advance for weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Drive ~30 minutes north to the Algarve interior. Visit Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar — one of the Algarve's most acclaimed wine estates. Book a morning wine tour and tasting (€15–25 per person) through their vineyards and modern winery. They produce excellent red, white, and rosé wines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the picturesque village of Alte (~45 min drive north) — considered one of the prettiest villages in the Algarve. Explore the cobblestone streets, traditional whitewashed houses with blue-tiled chimneys, and the natural spring (Fonte Grande). A peaceful, authentic Portuguese village experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel via Lagoa. Stop at Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery) in Guia (~20 min from hotel) for a late afternoon wine tasting if time permits (book ahead). Quiet evening at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — a relaxed Sunday morning start.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Zé in Alte — simple, authentic tasca (tavern) serving hearty Algarve mountain food. Try the roasted kid (cabrito assado) or the local chouriço. Budget ~€12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Self-catered or light dinner — pick up local wines, cheeses, presunto, and olives from a local supermarket or deli for a relaxed evening on the hotel terrace.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales must be booked in advance — check their website. Sunday opening hours vary for wineries. Alte is a 45-minute drive into the Serra do Caldeirão foothills — the road is scenic but winding.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia da Marinha or Praia do Carvalho (a hidden gem accessible via a tunnel through the cliffs, ~5 min from Marinha). Spend a leisurely morning swimming, sunbathing, and exploring the rock pools. Mid-September water temperature is perfect (~22–23°C).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive ~25 minutes east to Portimão — the Algarve's second-largest city. Visit the excellent Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, €3 other days) — a fascinating museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the Algarve's fishing heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its sardine grilling culture. Head to the riverside Largo 1° de Dezembro where local restaurants grill sardines on open charcoal grills — the aroma is irresistible. Enjoy the lively Monday evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local café near Carvoeiro.
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha or a picnic on the cliffs.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão riverside — excellent grilled sardines, fresh fish, and local wines. September is still sardine season. Budget ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Carvalho access involves a narrow tunnel — not suitable for those with claustrophobia. Portimão riverside has free parking in the evening. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely world-class — don't skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~1 hour east to Faro, the Algarve's capital. Start with the Cidade Velha (Old Town) — walk through the historic Arco da Vila gateway, visit the Sé Cathedral (climb the tower for views, €3.50), and explore the charming cobblestone streets and squares.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro marina to the Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro — part of the Ria Formosa Natural Park. The Ria Formosa is a stunning lagoon system of barrier islands, salt marshes, and tidal flats. Swim in the calm, shallow waters and spot flamingos and migratory birds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner. Explore the lively Rua de Santo António (pedestrian shopping street) and the evening café culture around Jardim Manuel Bivar.

meals.breakfast: Café Aliança in Faro — one of the oldest and most atmospheric cafés in the Algarve, established in 1908.
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Ilha Deserta — Estaminé restaurant is the only establishment on the island, serving fresh seafood with your feet in the sand. Budget ~€20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro Old Town — creative Portuguese cuisine in a beautiful historic building. Try the tuna with Algarve orange sauce. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Ilha Deserta departs from Faro marina — check seasonal schedules (September ferries run regularly). The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-protected area and a birdwatcher's paradise. Faro has good free parking near the marina.

day_by_day.morning: Drive ~1.5 hours east to Tavira — widely considered the most beautiful town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman Bridge, the Castle ruins (free entry, great views), and the charming old town with its distinctive four-sloped rooftops (a unique Tavira architectural feature).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry or water taxi from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a gorgeous barrier island with pristine, unspoiled beaches stretching for kilometers. The water is calm and shallow, perfect for swimming. Fewer crowds than western Algarve beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for dinner and evening exploration. Tavira has a sophisticated, less touristy feel than the western Algarve — enjoy the authentic Portuguese atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early start — grab breakfast at the hotel before the drive.
meals.lunch: Beach restaurant on Ilha de Tavira — try the grilled fish of the day with local salad and a glass of chilled Alentejo white wine.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bica in Tavira — beloved local institution serving traditional Algarvian cuisine. The arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) is exceptional. Budget ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a 1.5-hour drive from Lagoa — consider an early start. The town is beautifully preserved and far less commercialized than the western Algarve. Ilha de Tavira water taxi runs from Quatro Águas pier (~€2 each way).

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated wine tasting morning — drive ~20 minutes north to the Lagoa wine region. Visit Quinta da Penina or book a private tasting at a local quinta (estate). The Lagoa DOC wine region produces some of the Algarve's finest wines, particularly full-bodied reds from Negra Mole and Crato Branco grapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia de Marinha one final time for a proper afternoon of swimming and relaxation — by now you'll know the best spots and tide times. Walk the full 7km Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — one of Portugal's most spectacular coastal walks.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ferragudo — a gorgeous, authentic fishing village across the Arade River from Portimão (~20 min drive). Far less touristy than Carvoeiro, with a genuine local atmosphere and excellent seafood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a clifftop café during or after the coastal walk. Try a fresh salad and grilled chicken prego roll.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo — excellent riverside seafood restaurant with views of Portimão. Try the arroz de marisco (seafood rice) — a house specialty. Budget ~€22–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) is approximately 5.7km one-way — wear proper shoes and bring water. The trail runs from Praia da Marinha to Praia de Vale Centeanes. Ferragudo is a hidden gem — don't miss it.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Monchique — the Algarve's mountain retreat. Drive ~50 minutes north into the Serra de Monchique. Visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique (thermal springs), then continue up to Fóia peak (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve with spectacular 360° views over the entire region and the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Monchique town — browse the local artisan shops selling medronho (arbutus berry firewater), local honey, smoked sausages, and handmade wooden crafts. Walk to the ruins of the Franciscan Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast. Enjoy a final Friday evening in Carvoeiro — the village comes alive on weekends with a lovely local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the mountain drive.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — try the famous Monchique smoked pork (porco preto) and local mountain herbs. Budget ~€15–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — return to this favorite from Day 1 for a celebratory Friday dinner. Try the lobster rice if budget allows (~€35–45 per person) or the reliable grilled fish options (~€22–30).

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a completely different landscape from the coast — lush eucalyptus and cork oak forests, cooler temperatures. Buy medronho directly from local producers in Monchique — it's much cheaper and more authentic than tourist shops. The road to Fóia is narrow but paved.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — revisit your favorite beach of the trip or try Praia de Benagil one more time. Spend a leisurely morning swimming, reading, and soaking up the September sunshine. Water and weather conditions are still excellent.
day_by_day.afternoon: Shopping and souvenir hunting in Lagoa and Carvoeiro. Pick up: local Algarve wines (Lagoa DOC), almond and fig products (Dom Rodrigos sweets), local honey, dried herbs, handmade ceramics, and cork products. Visit the Lagoa Saturday market if timing works.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a memorable final evening meal celebrating 13 days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the local pastries and fresh orange juice one more time.
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — grilled fish at a beach snack bar or a simple café in Carvoeiro.
meals.dinner: Bon Bon Restaurant in Carvoeiro — one of the Algarve's finest restaurants, holding a Michelin star. Chef Louis Anjos creates innovative Portuguese tasting menus. Book well in advance. Tasting menu ~€85–110 per person. A splurge worth making for the final night.

day_by_day.notes: Bon Bon Restaurant requires advance booking — ideally book before the trip. If budget doesn't allow a Michelin dinner, Vila Joya in Albufeira (2 Michelin stars) or a high-quality seafood dinner at Sueste in Ferragudo are excellent alternatives at lower price points.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve. Take one last clifftop walk at Praia da Marinha to say goodbye to the stunning coastline. Pack, check out of the boutique stay, and load the car.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (~45 minutes). Return the rental car. Allow extra time for Sunday traffic and airport procedures. Depending on flight time, enjoy a final coffee and pastel de nata at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry memories of golden cliffs, turquoise waters, fresh seafood, and excellent Algarvian wines.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — a proper Portuguese breakfast of toast with butter and jam, fresh orange juice, and a bica (espresso).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café en route — or stop in Faro town for one last coffee if time allows.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time carefully — Faro Airport can be busy on Sunday afternoons in September. Return rental car with a full tank (petrol stations near the airport). Keep some euros for airport coffee and last-minute shopping. Portugal allows wine in checked luggage — pack your Lagoa DOC purchases carefully.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a swim among natural rock arches.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 13:00. Transfer from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min by private chauffeur transfer). Settle in, unpack, and enjoy a welcome drink on your terrace overlooking the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the clifftop path adjacent to Praia da Marinha to shake off travel fatigue. Admire the iconic golden limestone arches and turquoise coves from above before descending to the beach for a refreshing swim in the calm September waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace, followed by a refined welcome dinner showcasing Algarvian seafood and regional wines.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the boutique stay upon arrival – charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and a glass of chilled Vinho Verde arranged by the hotel.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Joya (Albufeira, ~20 min drive) – Two Michelin-starred restaurant offering a spectacular tasting menu with premium wine pairings; one of Portugal's finest dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer from Faro Airport. Request early check-in if possible so rooms are ready upon arrival. Vila Joya requires advance reservation – book months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim – Embark on a guided private coastal hike along the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail (Sete Vales Suspensos). Explore dramatic sea caves, natural arches, and hidden grottos unique to this stretch of the Algarve. Swim in secluded coves accessible only on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat tour departing from Benagil – sail along the coastline to explore the famous Benagil Sea Cave, Algar de Benagil, from the water. Continue to snorkeling spots around Praia de Carvalho and Praia do Caneiros aboard a premium catamaran with chilled drinks and fresh fruit on board.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a golden hour soak in the pool or a relaxing treatment at the in-house spa (if available). Pre-dinner glass of local Algarve rosé on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – freshly squeezed orange juice, açorda, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, and local honey.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch prepared by the hotel served aboard the boat – lobster rolls, grilled prawns, local olives, and chilled white wine.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Museu (Carvoeiro, ~10 min drive) – intimate, highly regarded restaurant known for exceptional grilled fresh fish, cataplana de marisco, and an impressive Portuguese wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat tour in advance through the hotel concierge. September waters are warm (~23°C) and ideal for swimming. Wear reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Quinta dos Vales Winery (Estômbar, ~20 min drive) – a premium Algarve estate offering an exclusive private morning tour of the vineyards, barrel cellar, and sculpture garden. Learn about indigenous Algarve grape varieties including Negra Mole and Crato Branco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Extended wine tasting session at Quinta dos Vales featuring their reserve and grand reserve labels paired with local charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and olive oil. Optionally purchase bottles to be shipped home. Return to the hotel for a relaxed poolside afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset catamaran cruise along the coast from Portimão – sip sparkling wine as the sun sets over the Atlantic horizon, with views of the Algarve cliffs glowing amber.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing lunch at Quinta dos Vales – curated by the winery's chef, featuring seasonal Algarvian produce matched to their finest vintages.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Sueste (Ferragudo, ~15 min drive) – romantic waterfront restaurant on the Arade River estuary, celebrated for its fresh grilled fish, seafood rice, and extensive Portuguese wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales private tours must be booked in advance. Arrange a driver for the day so both guests can fully enjoy the wine tasting without concern about driving.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cape St. Vincent (Cabo de São Vicente) – the southwesternmost point of Europe. Explore the dramatic windswept cliffs, the historic Fortaleza de Sagres, and the iconic lighthouse. Hire a private guide for historical context on Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Surf lesson or paddleboarding session at Praia do Martinhal near Sagres – one of the Algarve's most pristine and sheltered beaches, ideal for water sports. Alternatively, relax on the beach with a private cabana arrangement.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro area for a leisurely evening. Stroll through the charming village of Carvoeiro, browse artisan shops, and watch the sunset from the clifftop boardwalk.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: A Sagres (Sagres village) – a beloved local seafood restaurant serving the freshest grilled fish, barnacles (percebes), and local bread, paired with crisp Alentejo whites.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro, ~5 min drive) – one Michelin-starred restaurant offering a creative tasting menu blending Portuguese tradition with modern technique, and an exceptional wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1 hour 15 minutes from Praia da Marinha – hire a private driver for the full day. Bon Bon requires advance reservation. Cape St. Vincent can be windy; bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Kayaking and snorkeling tour along the Algarve grottos near Praia da Marinha and Praia do Carvalho – a private guided excursion through sea caves and arches accessible only by kayak. September light creates spectacular reflections inside the caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a luxurious spa afternoon – book a couples' massage, hydro-therapy session, or signature Algarvian treatment using local carob, fig, and almond extracts.
day_by_day.evening: Private chef experience – arrange through the hotel concierge to have a local Michelin-trained chef prepare a traditional Algarvian cataplana dinner in your suite or on your private terrace, paired with curated wines.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Post-kayak light lunch at Praia de Benagil beach bar – fresh grilled sardines, gambas al ajillo, and a cold Sagres beer or local rosé.
meals.dinner: In-villa private chef dinner – cataplana de marisco (shellfish stew), açorda de gambas, almond tart, and paired Algarve wines served on your terrace under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private chef experience at least 48 hours in advance through the concierge. The kayak tour is best done in the morning when seas are calm and light is optimal for cave photography.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Silves Medieval Castle (Castelo de Silves, ~25 min drive) – explore the best-preserved Moorish castle in the Algarve, with panoramic views over the Arade Valley and orange groves. Hire a private guide for an immersive historical tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming riverside town of Silves – visit the Gothic Cathedral, browse the Sunday market for local crafts, ceramics, and artisan food products. Stop at a local cork factory for an educational visit on Portugal's cork industry.
day_by_day.evening: Return via Lagoa town, stopping at a local pastelaria for a coffee and pastel de nata. Relax at the hotel before a fine evening out.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui (Silves) – a legendary Algarve institution serving exceptional grilled fish, monkfish rice, and shellfish platters in a convivial atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Praça (Lagoa, ~10 min drive) – elegant, contemporary Portuguese cuisine in a beautifully restored town square setting, with excellent regional wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: The Silves Medieval Festival typically takes place in August, but September retains the atmospheric charm without crowds. Silves is a UNESCO-listed historic town worth a full half-day.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private yacht charter departing from Portimão Marina – cruise the Algarve coastline at leisure aboard a luxury sailing yacht or motor yacht. Anchor at secluded beaches and coves inaccessible by land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht charter – swim, snorkel, paddleboard, and sunbathe on the open deck. The crew will serve a gourmet lunch on board. Explore the iconic Ponta da Piedade rock formations near Lagos from the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Dock at Lagos Marina and explore the vibrant historic town of Lagos – walk the medieval walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António, and enjoy aperitivos at a stylish waterfront bar.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before departure.
meals.lunch: Gourmet catered lunch aboard the yacht – fresh seafood, sushi-grade fish, salads, cheeses, chilled Vinho Verde, and sparkling rosé prepared by the yacht's private chef.
meals.dinner: No.1 Cocktail Bar & Restaurant (Lagos) – sophisticated rooftop bar and restaurant with panoramic views over Lagos Bay, offering premium cocktails and a refined modern Portuguese menu.

day_by_day.notes: Full-day luxury yacht charters cost approximately €1,500–€3,500 depending on vessel size. Book through a premium charter company such as Dream Yacht Charter Algarve or Algarve Luxury Boats. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure – sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast on your terrace, and take a private yoga or meditation session on the clifftops arranged by the hotel. A perfect recovery morning after the active yacht day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Portimão for a curated shopping experience – visit premium cork goods boutiques, hand-painted azulejo tile shops, and gourmet food stores for premium Algarvian products (local honey, almond sweets, carob products, premium olive oils).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at a clifftop bar in Carvoeiro, followed by a romantic dinner with sea views.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – enjoy at a leisurely pace with fresh fruit platters, smoked fish, artisan pastries, and specialty coffees.
meals.lunch: Tasca do Zé (Portimão) – a beloved local tasca serving authentic Algarvian home cooking: grilled sardines, piri-piri chicken, and traditional soups.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barão (Carvoeiro, ~8 min drive) – elegant clifftop restaurant with sweeping ocean views, known for its refined seafood dishes, premium steak options, and outstanding wine list.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberately relaxed day to balance the itinerary. The hotel concierge can arrange a private yoga instructor or wellness therapist to come to the property.

day_by_day.morning: Wine and olive oil tasting experience at Herdade dos Grous or Quinta do Francês (Alentejo border region, ~1 hr drive) – visit a prestigious estate producing award-winning reds and whites. Tour the vineyards, press house, and oak barrel cellar with a private sommelier guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the estate experience with a premium wine pairing lunch. Explore the surrounding countryside – rolling cork oak forests, cistus scrubland, and golden September light. Return to the hotel in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the boutique stay – enjoy the pool, order room service, or take a gentle walk along the clifftop path to watch the sunset.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Estate restaurant lunch at the winery – a seasonal tasting menu designed around their wine portfolio, featuring Alentejo black pork, local game, and regional desserts.
meals.dinner: In-hotel dining or room service – a curated selection of premium Algarvian dishes and local wines delivered to your terrace for a private, intimate evening.

day_by_day.notes: The Alentejo wine region is one of Portugal's finest and a worthy day trip. Arrange a private driver for the full day. Pre-book the winery visit to ensure the private sommelier experience is available.

day_by_day.morning: Stand-up paddleboard sunrise tour along the Praia da Marinha coastline – a guided small-group or private experience gliding past the golden cliffs and sea arches in the calm morning waters. September mornings are ideal with flat seas and soft light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ria Formosa Natural Park (east of Faro, ~1 hr drive) – take a private boat tour through the lagoon system, visiting barrier islands, flamingo colonies, and traditional fishing communities. Explore Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) for a swim on a pristine untouched beach.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back via Faro – explore the historic old town (Cidade Velha), visit the Cathedral rooftop for panoramic views, and enjoy a pre-dinner stroll through the cobbled streets.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the SUP tour – fresh juice, yogurt, and fruit arranged by the hotel for an early start.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Estaminé (Ilha Deserta, Ria Formosa) – a legendary restaurant on a protected barrier island accessible only by boat, serving extraordinary fresh seafood in a wild natural setting.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos (Faro) – housed in a beautifully restored 18th-century mansion in Faro's old town, offering refined regional cuisine with an exceptional Portuguese wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Restaurante Estaminé on Ilha Deserta is one of the Algarve's most unique dining experiences and requires advance booking. The Ria Formosa boat tour can be arranged as part of the same excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Private golf experience at Penina Hotel & Golf Resort or Amendoeira Golf Resort (~30 min drive) – play a round on one of the Algarve's championship courses. September offers ideal golfing conditions with warm temperatures and reduced summer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Post-golf relaxation – return to the hotel for a spa treatment or pool session. Alternatively, visit the Algar Seco rock formations in Carvoeiro for a dramatic cliffside walk and photo opportunity.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium evening – arrange a private beach dinner setup on Praia da Marinha at sunset (coordinate with the hotel), with a personal butler, white-linen table, candles, and a curated menu.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Clubhouse lunch at the golf resort – classic club sandwich, fresh salads, and a glass of chilled white wine overlooking the fairways.
meals.dinner: Private beach dinner on Praia da Marinha – a bespoke menu arranged by the hotel featuring grilled lobster, Algarvian seafood cataplana, Dom Pérignon champagne, and almond and fig desserts under a canopy of stars.

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner is the highlight of the trip – book at least 5 days in advance and confirm weather conditions the day before. A backup indoor terrace option should be arranged. Penina was designed by Henry Cotton and is one of Portugal's most historic courses.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia da Marinha – spend a leisurely morning on the beach with a private sunbed and parasol setup. Swim in the crystalline waters one last time, explore the rock pools, and soak in the spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive along the Algarve coast to Tavira (~1.5 hrs east) – one of the most beautiful and authentic towns in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, whitewashed churches, Moorish castle ruins, and the vibrant tile-decorated facades.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha for a final luxurious evening. Enjoy a premium wine tasting from the hotel's curated cellar – a vertical tasting of Algarve and Alentejo wines guided by a sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – indulge in the full spread on your final full morning.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Pátio (Tavira) – a charming courtyard restaurant in a restored townhouse, offering refined Algarvian cuisine including tuna tataki, clam cataplana, and local pastries.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) – return for a final Michelin-starred dinner, this time exploring the full tasting menu with the premium wine pairing option for a memorable farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is often called the most beautiful town in the Algarve and is worth the drive east. The evening wine tasting can be arranged through the hotel and is a perfect way to reflect on the wines discovered throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure – enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast on the terrace. Take one last walk along the clifftops of Praia da Marinha. Pack, check out, and collect any wine or artisan purchases made during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeur transfer to Faro Airport (~45 min). Depending on flight time, stop in Faro old town for a final coffee and pastel de nata, or browse the airport's premium duty-free for Portuguese wine, port, and gourmet products.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay – a special send-off spread with champagne, fresh fruit, pastries, and the hotel's signature dishes.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a Faro café or airport lounge – Portuguese cheese and charcuterie board, a glass of Douro white, and espresso.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 12:00 – request a late checkout if your flight is in the evening. Ask the hotel to arrange gift wrapping for any wine or artisan products purchased. Tip the hotel staff generously for an exceptional stay.
